prompt: Run /loop NEGOTIATE phase for sprint S01 of the config-diff epic. Generator proposes a contract, evaluator reviews it.
notes: Tests both generator-slice.md §1.5 (NEGOTIATE phase — module commitments in done_looks_like) AND evaluator-slice.md §1.5 (NEGOTIATE phase — reviewing contract draft).

assertions.text: Generator appended at least one entry to contracts.jsonl for sprint S01 (schema field is `sprint` per contract.schema.json)
Generator's contract entry has phase: agreed (NEGOTIATE-phase output)
Generator's contract has done_looks_like array with non-trivial content
Generator's contract has criterion_mapping covering all 4 cli archetype criteria (case-insensitive — spec.md uses Capitalized headers)
Generator commits to module identity (mentions specific module names like parser/differ/applier or similar)
Generator declares hides_decision at module level (per generator-slice.md §1.5 — sentence ≥30 chars naming a design decision)
Generator's contract is parseable JSON Lines (each line is valid JSON)
Evaluator references the generator's proposed contract (engaged with the actual content, not generic)
Evaluator cites at least one PASS criterion C1-C8 from foundation §3.5

Evaluator's review is NEGOTIATE-phase output (does NOT emit a structured `module_design_verification` JSON block — that's VERIFY-phase only). Mention-in-prose is allowed (and even desirable) to explain what NEGOTIATE skips.
Evaluator delivers a clear NEGOTIATE position: either approve or surface specific concerns
Evaluator references the §1.5 NEGOTIATE checklist items (C1 falsifiability, C4 entry-point budget, C5 two-adapter, §3 applicability, visible §5 red flags)
Evaluator does NOT enumerate all 8 PASS criteria (avoid false symmetry per foundation §3.5 'vocabulary not mandatory walk')
Generator uses the canonical per-module embedding shape from generator-slice §1.5 (MODULE <path> (applicability: ...))
Evaluator uses the NEGOTIATE severity vocabulary from evaluator-slice §1.5 (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / REJECT)
